transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because I just can't seem to keep myself together lately. Ever since my daughter left for basic training, I feel like I come home to a dead house, and it's really messing with me. 

It's getting bad. I'm sitting in my truck crying before my shifts start. At work, I'm missing steps on welding jobs I’ve done for years, and I've been snapping at the younger guys on the crew. And when I'm off the clock, I've just stopped going out on the water or working on my sculptures. I just don’t see the point right now. I need to figure out how to get my head back on straight.
Aside from your daughter leaving, have you experienced any other significant changes in your mood or energy levels that have persisted over the last two weeks or more?

No, not really. I mean... everything was pretty normal before she shipped out. I haven't noticed any other big changes in my mood or my energy besides what I just told you. It's really just been since she left that everything kind of went downhill.
Do you find yourself feeling physically restless, on edge, or worried about the future since your daughter left?

No, I wouldn't say that. I'm not pacing around or feeling jumpy or anything like that. And I'm not really worried about the future, either. I know she's going to do great in the military, she's a tough kid. It's just... I just feel really down and empty with her gone. But no, I don't feel restless or on edge.
Do you feel like you are experiencing any physical symptoms of anxiety, such as a racing heart, tightness in your chest, or difficulty breathing when you think about your current situation?

No, I don't think so. My heart isn't racing or anything like that. I don't feel tight in my chest, and I can breathe fine. It's really just that heavy, empty feeling I mentioned before, not a physical panic kind of thing.
Have these feelings of emptiness caused you to miss work or have they caused problems with your relationships with your coworkers?

I haven't been missing days, but... it is definitely affecting my work. I'm a sheet metal worker, and my supervisor actually had to take me off a complex welding job recently. He said I wasn't coordinating safely enough with the rest of the crew. 

And... I also do some metal sculpting on the side, and I just let a deadline for a submission pass without finishing the piece. I just couldn't get it done. So, yeah, it's definitely causing some real problems for me.
Since your daughter left, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your sleep patterns?

No, not really. I mean, my appetite is pretty much the same as it always is. I eat my regular meals. And my sleep hasn't really changed either. I still go to bed and wake up around the same times I usually do. It's just that heavy feeling I have during the day, but eating and sleeping are fine.
How long ago exactly did your daughter leave for basic training?
It's been about a month now since she left for basic training. And honestly, I've been struggling with this heavy feeling pretty much ever since she's been gone.
Do you feel that the level of distress you are experiencing is disproportionate to the situation of your daughter leaving for training?

I don't really know if it's disproportionate... I mean, I just know that it feels really bad. It's my daughter, you know? She's my only kid, and she's doing something dangerous, so it makes sense to me that I'd be worried. But... maybe it is a lot, since I can't even focus on my work. I'm not sure what's normal for this kind of thing.
Do you find yourself feeling like you are a failure, or do you have any persistent feelings of guilt about your daughter's situation or your own performance?

No, I don't think so. I don't feel like a failure. I mean, I raised a good kid, and I'm proud of her for enlisting, so I don't feel guilty about her being there. It's just hard that she's gone. And as for my job, I know my performance is slipping right now because I can't concentrate, but I don't feel like a failure as a person... I just feel really weighed down. But no, no guilt or anything like that.
